newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices hold with futures rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices hold with futures rally.

text.p: U.S. spot gas prices were steady to higher Tuesday despite expectations that cooler weather in the Northeast and Midwest would lead to continued softening, market sources said.
Helping to pump up prices was the rally of NYMEX's August gas futures to a high of $2.13, up 4.5 cents.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, physical prices rose about one cent to $2.17-2.18 per mmBtu at Henry Hub.
In south Texas, prices similarly edged one cent higher to about $2.11.
In the Permian Basin market, prices were at $2.03-2.06 early and as high as $2.09 shortly before nomination deadlines.
Southern California border prices rose two cents to $2.21-2.25 despite temperature highs in Los Angeles only in the high-70s F.
The 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 unit, in southern California, moved to about 56 percent power, while the adjacent unit 2, rated 1,070 MW, was running around 59 percent power.
In the Midwest, prices were also firm at $2.05-2.07, with Chicago city-gate gas holding at $2.23-2.24.
In the East, swing gas at the New York city gate prices were quoted little changed at $2.37-2.40 at M3 and Zone 6.
Separately, injection estimates for American Gas Association's storage report have ranged from 69 to 84 bcf.
